also: at this hour of the night

evidence: Traupman 88: at this time of night, hōc noctis
terms.comment: At night is noctū or nocte; late at night, multā nocte (see late at night); last night, proximā nocte (see last night); at this time of night, hōc noctis (Traupman 88).

evidence: Gell. 17.10.11: interdius fūmāre Aetnam, noctū flammigāre
terms.comment: The opposite of interdiū, by day.

terms.gloss: during the night, while it is still night
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.3.4: in comitium … dē nocte vēnit, in the night (Lewis & Short s.v. dē)
Hor. Ep. 1.2.32: ut jugulent hominēs, surgunt dē nocte latrōnēs (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 351: by night, noctū, dē nocte
terms.comment: Of what is done in the night hours, often before dawn, as robbers get up in the night. Traupman 86 also gives it for “after dark” and “in the dark”, which it does not mean (see after dark, darkness).

phrases.latin: sit nox cum somnō, sit sine līte diēs
phrases.english: let the night have sleep, and the day no quarrels

phrases.latin: nox ubi jam media est somnōque silentia praebet, et canis et variae conticuistis avēs
phrases.english: when it is midnight and the night offers silence for sleep, you too fall silent, dog, and you, many-coloured birds

phrases.latin: quis hic est homō, quem ante aedīs videō hōc noctis?
phrases.english: who is this man I see in front of the house at this time of night?
